active.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 29 at 3:31AM EDT by NWS Burlington VT

key_messages: Warm and breezy conditions expected across the region today ahead of a weak cold front. Some light rain showers will be possible tonight into Friday, with drier conditions returning for the weekend.
Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.
November will begin with dry, above normal temperatures, and remaining uncertain for the timing of precipitation in a week.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
650 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 224 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 224 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Warm and breezy conditions expected across the region today 
ahead of a weak cold front. Some light rain showers will be possible 
tonight into Friday, with drier conditions returning for the 
weekend.   

2. Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend. 

3. November will begin with dry, above normal temperatures, 
and remaining uncertain for the timing of precipitation in a week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 224 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A warm and breezy day is expected across the region 
today as southerly flow continues to usher in milder conditions. 
Afternoon high temperatures look to climb into the 60s areawide, 
with a few locations even nearing 70 degrees. A weak cold front will 
move through the region late today, bringing the potential for some 
light rain showers. The combination of weak forcing and some dry air 
to overcome will limit rainfall amounts, with most locations only 
observing a few hundreths of an inch. Strong cold air advection 
looks to take place on Friday behind the front, with increased 
clouds and some chances for showers in the favored upslope areas. 
Temperatures on Friday will be more seasonable, with highs in the 
upper 40s and 50s. 

Heading into the weekend, surface high pressure looks to build into 
the region once again. This will lead to another stretch of dry 
weather, with ample sunshine, light winds, and pleasant conditions 
to round out October and welcome the start of November. Temperatures 
on Saturday will be a little on the cooler side, with highs 
generally in the mid 40s to low 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Breezy winds and lower relative humidity values will 
lead to increased fire weather concerns over the next few days, 
especially given the plentiful dry leaves serving as fuel. Wind 
gusts today and Friday will generally be in the 15 to 25 mph range, 
with some higher gusts are possible. The highest winds gusts this 
afternoon are expected in the St. Lawrence Valley and northern 
slopes of the Adirondacks where gusts up to 35 mph are possible. 
Minimum relative humidity values will generally be between 40 to 55 
percent for both today and Friday. Heading into the weekend, minimum 
relative humidity values should drop into the 30 to 45 percent 
range, but winds look to be much lighter. A weak front moves through 
the region later today, bringing some light rain showers however a 
wetting rainfall is not expected.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Surface high pressure will shift offshore, but mid-level 
ridging will remain in place. Temperatures will move towards above 
seasonal norms, which is generally upper 40s to lower 50s during the 
day, and mid 20s to mid 30s at night as we enter into November. 
Instead, we'll have mid 50s to lower 60s during the days, and then 
mid 30s to mid 40s at night. A cold front is going to try to sink 
southwards Monday afternoon into Tuesday, but the upper vort is 
going to abandon the boundary and race east instead. So without cold 
air backing up the boundary and meager moisture, it may generate a 
few light rain showers, but that's about it. The pattern becomes 
increasingly uncertain after next Tuesday as a compact, but a strong 
upper low will begin to take shape in the Plains. The question 
is whether it completely cuts off from the jet stream or if it 
quickly gets absorbed back into the mid-latitude westerlies. 
Increasing ridging across the high latitudes will be present, 
and so this will likely keeps things moving slowly. Assessing 
forecast placement shows significant spread amongst different 
ensemble scenarios. So it's likely not worth hazarding a guess 
to when that rain exactly arrives until we see better certainty.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...Winds are beginning to increase across the
region. Conditions are VFR with pockets of stratus generally at
or above 6000 ft agl. South to southwest winds will become 
gusty between about 14z-23z, with the fastest winds at KBTV and 
KMSS. In general, surface wind speeds will range from 9-15 knots
with gusts reaching 17-25 knots at times. A cold front will 
shift northwest to southeast about 21z-05z. Along the front, 
there will be some light rain showers, as well as a reduction in
sustained winds and a gradual shift out of the southwest to 
west-southwest. This will result in pockets of LLWS for most 
terminals at some point in that window of time. Outside 
prevailing rain at KSLK and KMSS, the front is expected to 
decay, and so remaining terminals have PROB30s noted as the 
front shifts southeast. Ceilings will lower towards 2000-4000 ft
agl behind the boundary, with the greatest chances of MVFR 
ceilings at KSLK and KEFK. After 06z, winds will become more 
westerly around 5 to 10 knots.

Outlook...

Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&

.EQUIPMENT...
Routine observations from KSLK ASOS are unavailable until
further notice. While the site is operating, it is not able to
disseminate observations normally at this time. Technicians are
aware of the issue, but time of return to service is unknown.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
